Follow-up on [F\_262\_add\_diagram\_view.md](design/feature_descriptions/F_262_add_diagram_view.md), which is implemented.

Today the diagram agent generates a complete standalone SVG and MD² sanitizes it and injects it into the DOM. Replace that: the agent produces **JSON data** describing shapes and connections, and MD² owns rendering through React components.

* Diagram actions return a JSON file, not an SVG file.
* MD² renders the diagram with React components. Nodes are rendered by node components and connections by edge components.
* Support a fixed set of five diagram types instead of the skill's full catalogue.
* Data may carry position and size per item. When absent, MD² computes the layout itself with a simple algorithm.

## Why

* **Sanitizing disappears.** React builds the diagram from typed props. There is no agent-authored markup, so no parser, no attribute allowlist, and no injection surface. `diagram_svg_sanitizer.ts` and its tests are removed.
* **Interaction is a prop, not a convention.** Today the default diagram footer asks the agent to remember `data-diagram-id`, `data-diagram-label`, `tabindex`, and `role` on every drill-down item, and the app 
[5404 characters omitted]
Route edges ourselves as orthogonal paths with rounded elbows, fanning attach points along a shared edge.
* **Deterministic grid** — sequence needs no graph algorithm. Participants are columns, messages are rows; positions are arithmetic.

Keep layout behind a single `layout(data) => positioned` interface so an algorithm can be swapped or upgraded without touching the components.

## Removal of SVG diagram support

SVG is not a supported diagram format after this card. There is no dual-format period, no fallback, and no migration. Every code path that reads, writes, sanitizes, or describes an SVG diagram goes away, and diagram records written before this card are discarded on load rather than converted.

Delete outright:

* `app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_svg_sanitizer.ts` and `diagram_svg_sanitizer.test.ts`. Its only caller is `diagram_view_service.ts`.
* `desktop/src/actions/action/action_diagram_output.js` builds a `<label>-<timestamp>.svg` filename and rejects any returned `diagramPath` whose extension is not `.svg`. Both become `.json`.

Strip the SVG assumptions from what survives:

* `diagram_view_service.ts` — `currentSvg` and `currentSvgError` in the snapshot, `decodeSvgAsset` and its `image/svg+xml` content-type check, `loadSanitizedSvg`, and `loadActiveSvg`. Replaced by loading and schema-parsing the JSON document; rename the snapshot fields to match.
* `diagram_view.tsx` — the sanitized-markup injection, `handleSvgClick`, and `interactiveDiagramElement`, which locates a target by `closest('[data-diagram-id][data-diagram-label]')`. Replaced by rendering the typed diagram and handling clicks on the node and edge components directly.
* `DEFAULT_DIAGRAM_FOOTER` in `app/src/data/data_types.ts` — currently instructs the agent to produce standalone SVG, mark items with `data-diagram-id` / `data-diagram-label` / `tabindex` / `role`, and avoid scripts, `foreignObject`, links, and external resources. All of that is meaningless once the agent emits data. Rewritten to describe the JSON contract, the five supported types, and the field vocabulary.
* `app/src/data/action_placeholders.ts` — the `diagram-file` description reads “Absolute path where the current diagram action must save its SVG output.” The placeholder stays; the wording changes.
* Any test asserting on sanitizing, SVG parsing, `.svg` paths, or the old footer wording.

Leave alone: SVG support unrelated to diagrams, such as card images in `asset_paths.ts`, `card_image_operations.ts`, and the desktop MIME tables. Those serve other features.

The `diagramPath` plumbing through `action_run_registry.ts`, `action_run_types.ts`, `action_prompt_draft_service.ts`, `electron_action_bridge.ts`, and `action_popup_operations.ts` is format-agnostic and stays as is.

## Current state

F\_262 is implemented and this card replaces part of it:

* `app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_index.ts` stores a `DiagramRecord` per diagram with a repository-relative `path`. The record shape survives; the file it points at becomes JSON instead of SVG.
* `app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_view_service.ts` owns records, active path, popup state, and persistence. Structure is largely unchanged; the load-and-validate step swaps sanitizing for schema parsing.
* `app/src/components/diagram_view/diagram_view.tsx` owns the breadcrumb, Back button, FAB, context menu, and the diagram viewport. Everything except the viewport stays.
* `{{diagram-file}}` continues to resolve to the generated file path; only the expected format and extension change.

See the removal section above for what each of these loses.

Breadcrumb navigation, drill-down through `{{parent-node}}`, root and child action types, the diagram FAB, and the index tree all stay as they are.

## Out of scope

* User repositioning and resizing of diagram items. Planned for the next iteration, which is why position and size live in the data from the start and why the renderer must honour them when present. Persisting user edits back into the JSON is that card's problem, not this one.
* Any diagram type beyond the five listed.

Read `diagram_data.ts`, `diagram_layout.ts`, `diagram_view_service.ts`, `data_types.ts` (footer), `diagram_data.node.test.ts`, F_267. Findings first, then two questions.

**Origin.** Not in spec. F_267 mentions "complexity budget" only as prose in the diagram-design skill's `references/type-*.md`, listed as *design guidance for box anatomy and connector semantics*. Someone turned that prose into hard validation errors in `validateComplexity` (`app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_data.ts:335`). No card asked for it.

**Real technical pressure exists — but not in the parser.** Layout throws:
- `bestRoute` (`diagram_layout.ts:330`) throws `no unobstructed route exists` / `no non-overlapping route exists` when its lane candidates all fail. Routing is greedy sequential against `priorEdges`, so failure odds climb with edge count.
- `portPoint` (`diagram_layout.ts:256`) throws `too small for distinct connector ports` when fan-in/out exceeds side length / 8px.
- `MAX_DEPENDENCY_RANKS = 4` (`diagram_layout.ts:187`) — a second undocumented cap.
- `graphComponents` (`diagram_layout.ts:126`) computes transitive closure by n repeated passes over all nodes × destinations × transitives — roughly O(n⁴). Fine at 9 nodes, unusable at 100.
- `diagram_view_service.ts:106` runs `layout()` inside the parse path, so any layout throw becomes `currentDiagramError` and the whole diagram shows nothing.

So caps hid layout fragility instead of fixing it. Also: `DEFAULT_DIAGRAM_FOOTER` never told the agent about the caps → agent emits 12 nodes → hard reject → diagram lost.

The limits are real, undocumented, and were never requested. They live in two files.

`app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_data.ts` declares eight constants and enforces them at the end of `parseDiagramData`, inside `validateComplexity` and `validateSequenceFragments`:

* `MAX_NODES = 9`, lowered to `MAX_ENTITY_NODES = 8` for entity diagrams and `MAX_SEQUENCE_NODES = 5` for sequence diagrams.
* `MAX_EDGES = 12`, raised to `MAX_DEPENDENCY_EDGES = 14` for dependency diagrams.
* `MAX_ARCHITECTURE_GROUPS = 3`.

Read spec + both source files + both test files. Answer to card question first, then plan.

## Answer: was there a technical reason?

Yes — but layout-robustness, not data-validity. Confirmed in code:

- `bestRoute` (diagram_layout.ts:324) picks lowest-penalty candidate, then throws if that candidate still crosses a node or overlaps a prior edge. Routing is greedy/sequential, so failure odds climb with edge count. Edge caps hid this.
- `portPoint` (:240) throws when `sideLength / (ports+1) < PORT_GAP` (8px). A 24px terminator holds 2 ports. Node/edge caps hid this.
- `graphComponents` (:128) does `nodeIds.length` closure passes, each walking node × destinations × transitive → ~O(n⁴). Invisible at 9 nodes, blocking at hundreds.
- `MAX_DEPENDENCY_RANKS` (:27) guards nothing but aesthetics.

So the caps were load-bearing for layout, not for correctness. Fix belongs in layout.

## Change Plan — 6 blocks

**Block 1 — strip parser caps** (`diagram_data.ts`)
Delete 8 `MAX_*` constants, delete `validateComplexity` + its call. In `validateSequenceFragments` keep only: sequence-only rule, alt=2 regions / opt+loop=1 region, no duplicate edge in one fragment; drop count cap and the "both opt or loop" rule. In `validateTypeSpecificData` drop the 3-exit decision ceiling, the single-`cycle` ceiling, the `edges > nodes*2` state ceiling. Keep both label rules and all schema/reference/geometry checks.

**Block 2 — layout stops throwing on size** (`diagram_layout.ts`)
Remove `MAX_DEPENDENCY_RANKS` + throw in `layoutLayeredNodes`. Delete the two throws after `bestRoute`'s ranking — return lowest-penalty candidate as-is. `portPoint` clamps instead of throwing: ports distribute across the side and may coincide when spacing < `PORT_GAP`.

**Block 3 — `bestRoute` scores once**
Rewrite: score each candidate into an array once, take the minimum, instead of calling `routePenalty` from inside a sort comparator (which rescores O(n log n) times). Same winner, same tie-break order (first candidate wins ties, matching the current stable sort).

**Block 4 — iterative SCC in `graphComponents`**
Replace the repeated-pass transitive closure with an iterative Tarjan pass (explicit stack, no recursion, so deep graphs cannot overflow). Same output shape: `componentByNode` + `count`; `cycle` edges still ignored. `graphRanks` unchanged.

**Block 5 — label placement degrades** *(not in the spec's implementation section — flagging it)*
`edgeLabelPlacement` (:623) still throws `no collision-free label position exists for edge <id>`. That directly breaks the acceptance criterion "`layout` never throws for a document that `parseDiagramData` accepted" — and it is now reachable, since a 4-branch labelled decision node is exactly what Block 1 legalizes. Proposal: fall back to the longest-segment placement rather than throwing. `validateSuppliedRoute` throws stay — those are author-supplied waypoint errors, genuine data faults the parser cannot check.

**Block 6 — tests**
- `diagram_data.node.test.ts`: drop the `'nodes has more than 9 items'` assertion + 10-node fixture, rename test to "rejects invalid type semantics and geometry".
- New parser test: 40+ nodes, 60+ edges, >3 focal, >3 groups parses; sequence doc with 3 fragments incl. `alt` parses.
- New parser test: 4-exit labelled decision, multi-`cycle` dependency, state diagram with edges > 2× nodes all parse.
- `diagram_layout.node.test.ts`: dense graph with a necessarily-obstructed edge lays out, every input edge present in output; 24px state terminator with high fan-in positions rather than throws; dependency graph deeper than 4 ranks lays out; 100-node/150-edge diagram completes under a second.

Verify: `npm run typecheck` + vitest on `app/src/services/diagrams/` only.

Approve? Block 5 is the one judgment call — say if you want it left alone.
